what_happened: Direct reading of docs/architecture/orchestrate-state-machine.md (named in the dispatch's surface list) surfaced a load-bearing gap beyond stale prose: the stall_suspected detector is explicitly commit-gated and will undercount for plan-phase, specs-only dispatches under the new ignored posture, while the sibling stranded_suspected detector already covers that case by design (not commit-gated). Documented in the research report as the highest-priority surface, with a documentation-only fix (naming which existing detector covers it) rather than a code-change request.

The dispatch's named surface list (rules/state-management.md, rules/artifact-formats.md) was assembled by grep per the dispatch's own caveat; direct reading found neither file contains any specs-is-committed invariant assertion, so both were dropped from the recommended edit set in the research report rather than scoped for a planning phase.

The research report's explicit clearing of two dispatch-named surfaces (rules/state-management.md, rules/artifact-formats.md) as needing no edit removed two phases of wasted work from this plan before it was written; its 'verify each named surface by reading' finding was directly actionable at plan time.

Two gate collisions had to be discovered at plan time rather than inherited from research: rules/git-workflow.md is eager-loaded with only 1,128 B of headroom under Gate 20's 71,600 B baseline (so the Commit Timing addition carries a hard 400 B budget and a before/after measure-eager-context.sh --check), and four edit targets carry index-entries.json line_count rows whose Rule R drift is commit-blocking via Gate 3. The latter was initially invisible because index-entries.json stores paths relative to context/, so a grep for the full source-store-relative path returned zero rows.

validate-artifact.sh flagged five warnings on the first plan draft: four Files-to-modify wrapped-continuation lines beginning with a backtick (read as prose, not entries) and one Tier Justification under-verification, because the phase-5 selector run had been done over a 2-path subset rather than the phase's whole 6-path declared set. Fixed by rewording the continuations and re-running suite_selection_select once over the full set; second validation pass clean at 0 warnings.

Phase 4's Scope Hypothesis claimed planning-workflow.md has no 'Git Commit Failed' error template (only research-workflow.md matched that exact heading). Live check found all three process-workflow files DO carry an error template, just worded 'Git Commit Failure' (planning, implementation) vs 'Git Commit Failed' (research). Applied the third edit to all three for consistency rather than skipping two.

Phase 5's verify-touched.sh (23-suite named set) reported 2 failures: test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh (TIMEOUT at 600s bound; a pre-existing documented known-failures.txt entry, load-sensitive/'simply slow' at 543s hinted cost, unrelated to any doc content) and test-lint-agent-contracts.sh (one positive-check assertion about an unrelated agent-frontmatter fixture, re-ran clean in isolation immediately after -- a transient concurrency flake, not reproducing). Neither suite touches the docs this phase edited. All other 21 named suites plus the full 98-suite OWED fallback (unmapped index-entries.json path) passed.
git-commit-phase.sh dropped 'agent-system/extensions/core/context/standards/git-integration.md' from a phase commit pathspec: not contained in this task's declared file_scope.
git-commit-phase.sh dropped 'agent-system/extensions/core/context/workflows/preflight-postflight.md' from a phase commit pathspec: not contained in this task's declared file_scope.
